rule_policy.primary: Style direction applied within its trigger and exceptions.
rule_policy.contextual: Composition option evaluated against the content and presentation brief.

rules.name: Evidence-led result hierarchy
rules.trigger: A result slide supports an interpretable finding.
rules.decision: Make the supported finding easy to locate beside readable evidence.
rules.execution: Use a title, subtitle or adjacent explanation according to the content. Preserve uncertainty, scope and units.
exceptions: Setup and methods slides may need a topic title instead of a finding.
validation: The statement is supported and its qualifiers remain visible.

rules.name: Concise scientific explanation
rules.trigger: A figure needs explanation in a research talk.
rules.decision: Prefer concise interpretation to a full caption on the main slide.
rules.execution: Retain the method, comparison, evidence and reasoning this audience needs on the main slides, together with scientific qualifications and sources. Organize substantial content through hierarchy and explanatory graphics; concise interpretation does not mean a headline without its support. Trace only supplementary detail to notes or an appendix. For a short talk, select a coherent scope before stripping detail from every topic.
exceptions: Live technical verification can require a complete caption or derivation.
Essential interpretation details stay visible.
validation: Explanation, evidence and qualifications can be read together. The visible sequence provides enough reasoning for the selected depth; preserving the full source in notes does not by itself pass this check.

rules.name: Comparable dimensions
rules.trigger: A slide compares alternatives, mechanisms, conditions, results or groups of considerations.
rules.decision: Make the actual comparison clear through shared criteria where valid, explicit group identities and consistent visual encoding.
rules.execution: Use comparison-patterns.md to consider branched considerations, shared-criterion pairs or parallel qualitative fields, then choose by the actual comparison and source evidence. Design a different composition when those patterns do not fit. Align criteria, scales, units, label conventions and reading order; keep unequal baselines explicit. Preserve the distinction between two alternatives and benefits/constraints of one alternative. Quantitative indicators require verified comparable values and an encoding that preserves precision and uncertainty. Retain source-supported explanations and qualifications rather than filling a fixed number of rows or visual slots.
exceptions: Alternatives may require different amounts of evidence or unmatched controls.
Two sides, equal lists, a comparison badge, segmented bars and a fixed criterion count are optional; do not invent values, rankings, pairings or considerations to fit them.
validation: The layout does not imply scientific equivalence that the source does not support.

The composition makes the actual criteria and conditions inspectable, preserves all alternatives and source associations, and uses quantitative marks only when values, units, scales and precision support them.
An unsuitable pattern is replaced with a content-led design, with separately reviewed native editability, rendered appearance and retained-text continuity where relevant.

rules.name: Stable context with focused emphasis
rules.trigger: A sequence explains components of one framework.
rules.decision: Retain orientation while emphasizing the current component.
rules.execution: Keep meaningful labels and context stable; choose emphasis from the actual progression.
exceptions: Independent topics may need a fresh composition.
Do not imitate overlapping animation states.
validation: The listener can locate the current topic in the framework.

rules.name: Relationship-driven composition
rules.trigger: Content has a scientific relationship to explain.
rules.decision: Let comparison, mechanism, hierarchy or time determine the composition.
rules.execution: Choose a reading order and native objects that expose the relationship.
exceptions: A mandatory template can constrain arrangement.
validation: Connections and groupings match the source science.

rules.name: Section arrow navigation
rules.trigger: The listener needs orientation in a section sequence, or a slide already contains section navigation.
rules.decision: Use meaningful section arrows with restrained emphasis when orientation is needed, with no more than five items in a section navigation ribbon. Group studies with more sections under at most five truthful higher-level labels while preserving every scientific section and its topic content. Keep navigation items compact and visually connected; arrow segments should join closely with only narrow, consistent separators. Whenever a section navigation bar is present, always place it above the slide title and vertically center its native editable labels within the navigation shapes. Navigation labels must have an effective font size of at least 12 pt.
rules.execution: Retain useful existing navigation within the five-item limit. When the study has more sections, choose truthful higher-level groups and map every subsection to its appropriate group in the private design specification; highlight the group containing the actual current section. Do not drop scientific sections, truncate arbitrarily to the first five items, hide additional sections behind an ellipsis or add a second concurrent ribbon to bypass the limit. Reserve a distinct row above the title. Keep adjacent arrow segments tightly joined and judge visible tip-to-notch seams in the render; a small overlap of shape frames may be needed. Fit the bar through concise label wording, segment widths, overall placement or coherent reflow within the five-item limit, without widening the gaps to fill the row or obscuring labels. Keep native editable labels at 12 pt or larger after inheritance, automatic fitting and group scaling; do not shrink them to resolve a fit problem. Keep repeated label frames, positions, insets, font family, size and weight fixed across slides; use color or fill for active emphasis so the words do not move as the section changes. Inspect rendered label alignment and fit. Navigation labels use the role-based middle anchoring in R016. Key takeaways do not need a dedicated ribbon item; use a truthful concluding group or omit navigation on that summary.
exceptions: Navigation is optional on covers and self-contained pages; the placement rule does not require adding a navigation bar.
Do not invent an unrelated sequence.
validation: The ribbon contains no more than five navigation items, with no ellipsis or secondary concurrent ribbon used to bypass the limit.

Section names or higher-level groups and emphasis match the talk structure. Every scientific section and its topic content remain represented; when grouping is needed, the private mapping covers every subsection and the current section belongs to the highlighted group.
Every section navigation bar is above the slide title, with a visible separation between the two roles.
Navigation items form a compact group. Arrow segments read as a continuous strip with narrow, consistent visible seams and legible labels.

Native editable navigation labels use vertical middle anchoring with consistent internal insets and readable fit in the delivery application. Their effective size remains at least 12 pt after inheritance, automatic fitting and group scaling, without shrink-to-fit.
Repeated words retain their visible positions when the active section changes: label frames and font metrics remain consistent, with color or fill carrying the active emphasis.

rules.name: Teal and scientific color roles
rules.trigger: A palette or emphasis color is needed.
rules.decision: Use teal or a requested scientific palette with deliberate semantic roles.
rules.execution: Preserve category mappings; pair color with labels and markers; check contrast.
exceptions: Scientific figure colors and existing legends take priority.
Operational hex values are adjustable, not a prescribed journal palette.
validation: The palette is legible and every changed mapping has a consistent legend.

rules.name: Conceptual part markers
rules.trigger: A subject is explained through multiple conceptual parts.
rules.decision: Use title markers such as (1/3) to identify conceptual progress.
rules.execution: Count conceptual parts, which may span more than one page. Preserve useful existing markers.
exceptions: Do not invent a denominator or renumber by slide count.
validation: Markers match the explanation structure.

rules.name: Context before density
rules.trigger: A presentation is being designed or transformed.
rules.decision: Resolve audience, available time and technical depth before choosing density.
rules.execution: Reuse named profiles and the current purpose. Ask only consequential missing information.
exceptions: Analysis-only work needs no invented talk context.
Current instructions override defaults.
validation: The design matches the brief without silently losing checkable detail.

rules.name: Crisp and considered diagrams
rules.trigger: A diagram or explanatory visual needs design work.
rules.decision: Use readable labels, adequate resolution and intentional color.
rules.execution: Prefer native editable relationships when reconstruction is verified. Preserve complex figures otherwise.
exceptions: Upscaling does not recover missing detail.
A visual technique is judged by its role rather than a blanket ban.
validation: Labels are readable and scientific relationships remain correct.

rules.name: Connected explanation and comparable information
rules.trigger: Drafting or reviewing documentation, transformation reports or presentation wording.
rules.decision: Develop continuous reasoning in natural paragraphs; use tables for discrete information that benefits from shared comparison criteria.
rules.execution: Explain the design choice, its reason and any limiting condition. Follow writing-style.md; preserve sufficient context and exact scientific or technical qualifications. For slide wording, follow writing-style.md#research-slide-wording: lead with the actual topic or source-backed finding, proofread labels and terminology, and keep qualifications, attribution and cross-references accurate.
exceptions: Ordered procedures retain their sequence; commands and schemas retain literal syntax.
Labels, equations and slide text use the form and length appropriate to their purpose.
validation: The reader can follow how the explanation develops and why the design choice fits the content.
Tables organize genuinely discrete information without fragmenting a continuous argument.
Slide wording preserves precise terms, qualified claim strength, first-use definitions and source identities rather than replacing them with filler or unsupported conclusions.

rules.name: Space as structure
rules.trigger: Composing or reviewing the hierarchy and spatial relationships of a slide.
rules.decision: Use proximity, distinct group intervals and surrounding space to express the reading order and relationships in the research.
rules.execution: Follow spacing-and-hierarchy.md. Judge typography, visible object edges, outer margins and repeated gaps together at the intended display size; adapt proportions to the actual canvas.
exceptions: Dense technical evidence can require compact spacing while labels and scientific qualifications remain readable.
Mandatory layouts and comparison axes constrain rearrangement; preserve evidence associations and scales.
External brand ratios and UI spacing tokens are references, not universal slide presets.
validation: Related evidence, labels, units and qualifications remain visibly associated.
Groups, hierarchy and reading order are clear without forcing all gaps to be equal.
Spacing remains coherent across related slides and readable at the intended display scale.

rules.name: Fira typography and readable size hierarchy
rules.trigger: Applying Sherry's style to slide text or reviewing text legibility.
rules.decision: Use Fira Sans titles and a deliberate size hierarchy, with no displayed text below 10.5 pt and section navigation labels at least 12 pt.
rules.execution: Follow design-system.md: use a suitable Fira title variant, usually Extra Condensed Bold, and Fira Sans for Latin body text. Usually use 12 pt body text and 16 pt prominent subheadings, reserving 10.5 pt for minor information. Section navigation labels retain the separate 12 pt minimum in R007. Resolve actual fonts beyond theme defaults; check script coverage and effective sizes after fitting and scaling. Rearrange or split content rather than shrinking below the floor.
exceptions: An explicit current typography requirement takes precedence over style defaults.
Other scripts and mathematics need suitable fonts and preserved notation; do not force an unsupported Fira substitution.
Raster labels need separate review at final placed size. Retain scientific fidelity and report an unresolved legibility limit instead of claiming a native-size pass.
validation: Titles use the intended Fira family or an explicitly resolved alternative, without a silent Arial or Calibri substitution.
Native text, tables, chart labels, legends, units and footnotes meet the size floor after fitting and scaling.
The final render preserves readable evidence and scientific notation; image interiors are not certified by a text-style inventory.

rules.name: Symmetric work area and separate slide number
rules.trigger: Defining a slide master, laying out slide content or checking content boundaries.
rules.decision: Establish a centered rectangular work area before placement and keep all foreground content inside it except the slide number.
rules.execution: Record bounds and units for the actual canvas, with equal left/right and equal top/bottom margins. Include titles, navigation, figures, labels, explanations, citations and footnotes. Place the slide number outside the work area at the bottom right, black on light backgrounds and white on dark backgrounds. Use matching master or layout guides through a suitable native workflow.
exceptions: Slide backgrounds may fill the canvas; they are not foreground content.
An explicit current mandatory template or requested layout takes precedence; explain a conflict rather than silently changing its boundaries.
A coordinate example does not establish universal dimensions across different canvases.
validation: The private design specification records a symmetric work area that fits the actual slide.
Visible foreground extents, including groups, rotations, connectors and overflowing text, remain inside it.
The slide number is the only foreground exception and has the required bottom-right position and black or white color.

rules.name: Stable text starts and content-aware table alignment
rules.trigger: Formatting text boxes or native table cells.
rules.decision: Top-anchor unfilled body text, captions and free-standing headings. Vertically center flowchart-node text, filled text boxes, navigation labels and table cells within their intended text regions. Preserve established title anchoring and keep retained logical text fixed across consecutive slides. Left-align descriptive table text and center short entries, including numbers.
rules.execution: Follow design-system.md#text-boxes-and-tables. A text box over a separate bounded background shape counts as filled for this rule; a whole-slide background does not. Center its designated text region with balanced vertical insets, rather than centering every element in a multi-object panel as one block. Top-anchored roles retain matched top edges, insets and first-line metrics. For retained text of either anchor type, lock frame geometry including height, font metrics, wrapping and insets across consecutive slides. Changing a centered container height must not move unchanged text. Treat horizontal alignment separately, and use native authoring for properties beyond the bounded helpers. Inspect final native properties and adjacent renders.
exceptions: An explicit user-specified layout can override the role-based default; preserve scientific readability and retained-text continuity.
Title layout remains established; a large colored panel does not make its figures and independent text regions one centered text box.
validation: Unfilled body text is top-anchored; flowchart nodes and filled text regions, navigation and table cells are middle-anchored with readable fit.
Retained text does not move across adjacent renders, including within middle-anchored nodes.
Table horizontal alignment follows content: descriptive text left, short entries centered, right alignment only on explicit instruction.

rules.name: Considered design for substantial text
rules.trigger: A slide contains a substantial text block or a dense explanation.
rules.decision: Give the text a visible design treatment and a clear internal hierarchy that helps the audience follow the explanation.
rules.execution: Use a meaningful heading, restrained accent rule, background treatment or labeled grouping with deliberate spacing according to the content. Keep continuous reasoning in connected prose and retain essential scientific qualifications with their evidence. Judge the treatment, type hierarchy and available space together. Grouping and enclosure do not by themselves satisfy R024; assess the explanation for a useful object depiction, relationship or comparison.
exceptions: Short labels and captions can remain plain.
A mandatory template can constrain the available treatment; improve hierarchy within its requirements.
validation: Substantial text has a clear entry, readable grouping and purposeful visual treatment.
The treatment supports the scientific reading order without obscuring evidence, adding unsupported meaning or losing qualifications.
Text and its treatment remain within the work area, with the required size floor and comfortable internal spacing.

rules.name: Soft neutral panels for contained explanations
rules.trigger: A self-contained explanation needs a visible boundary or separation from neighboring evidence.
rules.decision: Consider a light gray fill with gentle corner rounding when it clarifies the explanation's grouping.
rules.execution: Evaluate fill, corner shape, insets, heading hierarchy and surrounding space together using design-system.md#choosing-a-text-box-treatment. Keep shared treatments coherent across comparable blocks, preserve evidence associations and use appropriate native authoring for changes outside a helper's operation set. A soft panel is a grouping choice, not a substitute for the semantic visual contribution required by R024.
exceptions: Labels and captions may communicate their association more clearly without a filled enclosure.
Dark backgrounds need an appropriate neutral tone and checked contrast.
External consulting examples inform grouping decisions without prescribing a universal corner shape or brand palette.
validation: The treatment creates a meaningful group without crowding the text or competing with the evidence.
Internal clearance, role-based anchoring and stable retained-text positions, the type-size floor and the symmetric work area remain intact.

rules.name: Two table-color choices after inspection
rules.trigger: The deck contains tables and the current table-palette decision is unresolved.
rules.decision: Offer Nature-inspired and deck-matched color treatments of the same representative table for the user to choose.
rules.execution: Follow design-system.md#table-color-options and guided-intake.md. Use the reference-defined Nature-inspired preset with warm stone headers, white body cells, black text and horizontal rules without a vertical grid. Keep content, layout, fonts, numeric precision and emphasis targets identical in both previews. Present exactly two preset choices through the available tool and wait for a submitted choice or explicit delegation before final table coloring. Record and reuse the resolved choice privately for comparable tables.
exceptions: Reuse an explicit current choice or delegation; do not ask for a deck without tables.
Existing scientific category, heatmap, sign and significance mappings remain protected in both options.
A mandatory template can constrain the permitted color changes; a design preview does not establish native editability.
validation: The alternatives differ in color treatment while their scientific content and other design decisions match.
The final table palette follows the actual resolved choice rather than a preselection or elapsed time.
Contrast, labels, semantic colors and the established alignment and size rules remain sound.

rules.name: Readable quantities and consistent table precision
rules.trigger: Formatting displayed quantities in slide text, tables or chart labels.
rules.decision: Group quantity values with four or more integer digits and keep decimal places consistent for comparable values in a table.
rules.execution: Follow scientific-fidelity.md#numeric-display. Preserve raw values, formulas and unrounded data separately from display strings. Use comma grouping unless an explicit locale requires otherwise, choose a supported precision for comparable quantities and record meaningful exceptions. Changes beyond the bounded helpers require native authoring and source-to-display review.
exceptions: Years, dates, identifiers, references, codes, versions and mathematical notation retain their meaning and syntax.
Different units, quantity types, significant figures and measurement resolution can justify different precision within a table.
Small nonzero values, p values, uncertainty and thresholds need suitable source-supported notation; uniform decimals must not create false zeros or unsupported precision.
Retained image text needs verified reconstruction or an explicit remaining-formatting limit.
validation: Grouping applies to quantities rather than a mechanical replacement of every four-digit token.
Comparable table values use a coherent display precision, with justified exceptions traceable to the source.
Displayed signs, units, inequalities, uncertainty and interpretations match the preserved raw values and formulas.

rules.name: Recurring branding through native master inheritance
rules.trigger: Comparable slide roles contain recurring logos or watermarks, with a possible isolated omission.
rules.decision: Restore intended recurring branding through native masters and layouts while preserving intentional slide-role exceptions.
rules.execution: Follow design-system.md#recurring-logos-and-watermarks and the native application workflow. Inspect existing assets, master/layout relationships and slide visibility overrides. Reuse the correct mark and restore the appropriate layout or inheritance rather than pasting individual copies. Review every affected slide after a shared change; preserve proportions, work-area bounds and unrelated template content. Use native authoring because the bounded helpers cannot repair masters or layout relationships.
exceptions: Covers, section dividers, full-bleed pages and deliberately unbranded layouts can differ; compare intended roles rather than assuming every absence is a defect.

Do not overwrite distinct brand variants, invent an asset, remove required confidentiality marks or enable all master graphics indiscriminately. Preserve intentional background watermark coverage and repetition under the background exception; foreground marks retain the work-area bounds.
If the intended treatment or native repair cannot be established, resolve the ambiguity or disclose the pending repair; do not claim inherited branding has been fixed.
validation: The intended branding appears on each applicable slide through the correct native master or layout, without unintended duplicates.
Shared changes preserve intentional exceptions, unrelated objects, content visibility and editability.
Every affected rendered slide is checked for missing or duplicate marks, overlap, contrast and unintended propagation.

rules.name: Square brackets for unit labels
rules.trigger: A displayed quantity label explicitly includes a unit in slide text, a table, chart or figure.
rules.decision: Use square brackets for unit labels, such as Capacity [MW], Gain [%] and Temperature [°C].
rules.execution: Follow scientific-fidelity.md#unit-labels. Change only unit delimiters, preserving quantity meaning, values, unit symbols, case, exponents, scale factors, currency basis and denominators. Trace rewritten labels in the private content ledger, use native authoring beyond the bounded helpers and review the actual output.
exceptions: Ordinary inline values and units retain their natural form; do not wrap every unit occurrence.
Mathematical grouping, uncertainty, confidence intervals, citations, years and conceptual part markers such as (1/3) are not unit delimiters.
Labels in retained complex or raster figures need an available editable source or verified reconstruction; otherwise retain the figure and disclose the formatting limit.
validation: Editable quantity labels use square-bracket unit notation consistently within the task scope.
Only intended delimiters change; scientific units, associated values and unrelated parentheses remain accurate.
The content ledger and native render confirm label meaning, fit and readability; inaccessible image labels are not falsely reported as reformatted.

rules.name: Full terms at first visible abbreviation use
rules.trigger: A research abbreviation or acronym first appears in the audience-visible presentation sequence.
rules.decision: Give the verified full term at the first visible occurrence, then use the abbreviation consistently.
rules.execution: Follow writing-style.md#research-slide-wording and scientific-fidelity.md. Inspect titles, body text, tables, figures, legends and build stages in actual presentation order. Put the full term with the abbreviation or in an immediately associated visible explanation; a later glossary, appendix or speaker note alone is insufficient. Record the definition and first-use destination in the private content ledger and use native authoring for text changes beyond the bounded helpers.
exceptions: Use the source and research context to establish clear terms without unnecessary questions; unresolved definitions or material ambiguities need an actual answer before expansion.
SI unit symbols, chemical formulas, mathematical symbols, identifiers, codes and proper names are not automatically acronyms to expand.
A retained figure can receive an adjacent visible definition without altering its image text; repeat a definition when a section or slide must stand alone or the audience needs a reminder.
Exact protected quotations and source identities remain intact; add a separate explanation instead of silently rewriting them.
validation: Each research abbreviation has its correct full term at the earliest audience-visible occurrence, including relevant build states.
Definitions remain consistent within each scientific context. Distinct verified concepts sharing an abbreviation are visibly disambiguated, preserving protected source terms and identifiers.
Definitions, scientific notation, source attribution and native editability are reviewed separately from spelling and package checks.

rules.name: Intentional text and visual composition on every slide
rules.trigger: Creating, editing or reviewing any slide in the requested work scope, including pages that already contain figures or diagrams.
rules.decision: Give every in-scope slide an intentional, polished text and visual composition and an individual page review. Make the relevant research objects, distinctions, evidence or verified relationships visible. Assess splitting a complex explanation when useful graphics and readable text need more room.
rules.execution: Follow visual-storytelling.md and design-system.md#visual-treatment-for-every-slide. Review every in-scope page for the explanatory contribution, hierarchy, spacing and balance of its text and visual material, including method, result, comparison, question, cover and closing slides. Before filling a slide with prose, record the visual's explanatory purpose, role and source support privately. Distinguish evidence, explanatory schematics and illustrative depictions. Compose interacting objects, operations, states, constraints or comparisons at the resolution the source and audience need, with explanatory native labels and a stable visual vocabulary. A recognizable icon, repeated object or box-and-arrow layout does not by itself explain a method or mechanism. Text-only sources can support substantive analytical schematics without supplying numerical data. Prefer editable text, shapes and connectors; use coherent, adequately resolved assets when useful and disclose image-interior editing limits. Split at coherent conceptual boundaries when readability, spacing or distinct explanatory purposes justify it. Preserve sufficient visible method, evidence and reasoning as well as complete source-to-output coverage, essential qualifications and attribution; update notes, navigation and cross-references. Retain effective existing treatments, role-based anchoring and stable retained text, the type hierarchy including R007's five-item ribbon limit and 12 pt navigation minimum, and the symmetric work area. R017 and R018 establish grouping, not proof of an explanatory graphic.
exceptions: Exact proofs, quotations, references and necessary prose can retain their form when the purpose or scientific meaning requires it; record the slide-specific reason and still review typography and composition. Abstract methods and equations do not require a physical metaphor or a decorative icon.

Explanatory imagery must be distinguishable from research evidence. Do not invent causal, temporal, quantitative or categorical relationships; use an accurate nonrelational illustration or composition where possible when a relationship is unverified.

Do not impose a graphic quota, fixed slide count or split solely for decoration. A mandatory template may constrain treatment; record any necessary exception. Unavailable native authoring or review leaves the selected work pending rather than completed.
validation: Every in-scope slide has an individual composition review, including pages that already contain figures or diagrams. Identify the understanding contributed by its text and chosen visual material or document a slide-specific exception; panels, number badges, generic topic icons and arrows between unchanged paragraphs do not by themselves satisfy the rule, and there is no mandatory icon or picture quota.

The audience can follow the slide's required operation, changed condition, comparison or inference through the composition and its labels. Subject recognition alone is insufficient when a method or relationship needs explanation. Illustrations do not imply observations or results, and diagram connections, visual quantities, claims, qualifications and attribution remain source-supported.

Compare the visible narrative with the source for sufficient method, evidence and reasoning. Explain material relocation or scope exclusion privately. Reject sparse headlines supported only by notes, and reject rich-looking diagrams with unsupported details; neither icons nor word counts certify quality.

Any split preserves complete source-to-output coverage, reasoning order, essential qualifications beside their claims, and correct references, notes and navigation. The resulting slides have readable type and comfortable spacing rather than crowded graphics or smaller text.

Native editability and the final application render are reviewed separately. Visual assets have adequate resolution and consistent treatment, editing limits are disclosed, text starts remain stable, navigation follows R007, tables follow their rules, and content respects the work area and type-size floor.

rules.name: Research-led cover composition
rules.trigger: Creating or materially redesigning the cover of a research presentation.
rules.decision: Choose the focal subject and composition from the research identity and available trustworthy material, with deliberate quiet space and title hierarchy.
rules.execution: Follow cover-art-direction.md. Consider a subject in focus, place and scale, mechanism as identity or one idea expressed through a restrained form. Preserve the approved typography and scientific color meanings. Keep title and metadata editable, distinguish observed imagery from representative or conceptual imagery, and record the direction and source support privately. Compare another plausible composition internally when the initial result feels generic. Use Apple examples for compositional judgment rather than copying campaign assets, logos or visual effects.
exceptions: A mandatory institutional cover can constrain the composition; improve hierarchy and spacing within it.
A deliberate typography-led cover can be appropriate when imagery would add no understanding. No image, color scheme or cover questionnaire is mandatory.
Keep unverified subject details unresolved rather than inventing scientific imagery; unavailable native review remains pending.
validation: The cover establishes a recognizable research subject or idea through a clear focal hierarchy, rather than an interchangeable title frame.
Full-size and thumbnail review confirms intentional space, readable title and metadata, contrast and alignment within the foreground work area.
Scientific imagery is accurate for its stated role; text remains editable and the delivery application render has been reviewed.

rules.name: Purposeful and licensed icon sourcing
rules.trigger: An explanatory graphic needs an additional icon or asset beyond the available local set.
rules.decision: Choose a semantically appropriate, coherent asset through an available permitted route, with its actual license and credit preserved.
rules.execution: Follow asset-sourcing.md. Flaticon is an optional source through available permitted browsing or an explicitly configured official API. Inspect the depicted object and family, actual download permission and account entitlement. Use generic nonconfidential searches and keep an asset/source/license record privately. Retain required visible credits and verify the imported render. Use bundled icons or native drawing where online acquisition is unavailable. Do not assume a built-in API integration or redistribute downloaded stock in the skill package.
exceptions: Do not add an icon when it contributes no understanding or introduces an unsupported scientific detail.
A login, paid download or API dependency must be resolved through the available authorized workflow; it does not permit bypassing access or format restrictions.
Retained research figures keep their evidence role; an illustration is not a replacement for a result.
validation: The chosen asset depicts the relevant subject and fits a coherent visual family, with adequate placed resolution.
Actual source, license, required credit and slide destination are traceable; no private research was uploaded merely to search for an icon.
Reports distinguish a found page, a licensed download and a tested import. No unsupported API, account or redistribution capability is claimed.

rules.name: Flags as labeled country identifiers
rules.trigger: Several country-level results or comparisons would benefit from faster recognition.
rules.decision: Consider small verified flags paired with country names on selected slides, preserving readable quantitative comparisons.
rules.execution: Follow asset-sourcing.md#use-flags-to-aid-country-comparisons. Match the exact source geography and relevant time context, keep names or defined codes editable, and use consistent optical size with correct flag colors and proportions. Place each flag near its country and corresponding result. Use a licensed static asset rather than relying on platform-specific emoji.
exceptions: Omit flags when they crowd the evidence or add little recognition value; retain all country results and text identifiers.
Do not assign a country flag to a region, aggregate, ambiguous code or unmatched geographic entity. Preserve the source label while resolving a material ambiguity.
Flags do not replace legends, data marks, scales, heatmap colors or source scientific color mappings.
validation: Every flag-to-name-to-result association matches the source and is legible in the application render.
Country identity, source ordering, quantities, uncertainty and scientific color roles remain unchanged.
Flag source and reuse permission are recorded; proportions, colors, contrast and optical alignment remain coherent.

rules.name: Grouped and traceable figure panels
rules.trigger: A source composite figure or several related panels would be clearer as grouped evidence regions or a focused slide sequence.
rules.decision: Consider generous rounded color regions with native panel headings or badges, separating the evidence without separating it from its interpretation context.
rules.execution: Follow figure-panels.md. Inspect the whole figure and caption before extracting or cropping. Retain original panel identities, shared axes, legends, color bars, scale bars, uncertainty and citations. Keep any new deck-local A/B/C/D labels distinct and traceable; H identifiers require an established hypothesis identity or an explicitly confirmed presentation-group meaning that is visibly distinguished from a hypothesis. Use native framing and labels around retained panels, with complete source-to-output and crop-bound records. Prefer separate source objects or reversible crops; the optional pixel-crop helper does not detect panels or certify scientific completeness. Split at coherent boundaries when legibility needs more room.
exceptions: A shared axis, legend or connected relationship may require retaining the original whole figure or visibly repeating verified context.
The number of regions follows the actual explanation; four panels, equal cards and fixed corner radii are not required.

Do not remove observations, uncertainty or required context, stretch plots to fit equal cards, or imply a common experiment between unrelated studies. Retained image interiors remain raster or vector assets, not native scientific objects.
When exact H labels are requested without a clear meaning, clarify their role before presenting them as hypotheses; a request for badge styling alone can use neutral panel letters.
validation: Each destination panel maps to the original figure, panel label and exact crop or object; all dependencies needed for interpretation remain visible.
Reordering and color grouping introduce no unsupported scientific relation or comparison, and citations, notes and cross-references remain correct.
Native labels and framing remain editable; retained image limits are disclosed and every relevant application render is checked for fit and legible evidence.

rules.name: Visual key takeaways at the end of the talk
rules.trigger: Creating or refining a complete multi-slide presentation.
rules.decision: Conclude the main narrative with key takeaways that synthesize supported messages through meaningful visuals and concise wording.
rules.execution: Follow visual-storytelling.md#close-with-visual-key-takeaways. Use a closing slide or short sequence that reuses established research objects, verified relationships or legible evidence. Select the message count and composition from the argument, keep essential qualifications visible and retain native editable wording. Place optional Q&A, contacts or supplementary pages after the final substantive summary. Trace condensed statements to source and earlier evidence. The summary does not require a dedicated ribbon item; use an appropriate existing group or omit its navigation.
exceptions: A request limited to individual slides does not require an unrelated new ending.
Tutorials and proposed studies summarize learned concepts, supported questions or next steps without inventing completed findings.
Unavailable authoring or an unverifiable visual leaves the closing work pending; plain text is not reported as a completed visual synthesis.
validation: The complete talk has a final substantive key-takeaways summary before any Q&A or supplementary material.
Established objects, relationships or evidence contribute to recall; plain bullets, generic checkmarks and decorated text cards alone do not satisfy the rule.
Messages preserve claim strength, assumptions, uncertainty, proposed/completed status and attribution without introducing new results or unsupported recommendations.
The closing composition has deliberate hierarchy and space, readable evidence and editable wording, with separate scientific, editability and native-render review.

rules.name: Motivation, main question and related inquiries
rules.trigger: Creating or refining a Research Question page for a study with a central question and related inquiries.
rules.decision: Connect an illustrated research motivation with one dominant question and clearly differentiated subquestions.
rules.execution: Follow visual-storytelling.md#frame-a-research-question. Start with a narrow motivation strip at left, a prominent question callout at upper right and coordinated subquestion regions beneath it when that arrangement fits. Adapt research objects, wording, region count and placement to the actual source and canvas. Keep the main question visually dominant and enough explanation visible to distinguish each inquiry. Use source-supported relationships or a noncausal comparison/evidence gap; preserve hypotheses and findings as different roles. Keep text and framing native where feasible, retain the work area and text anchoring rules, and use the target palette and authorized master branding.
exceptions: Three motivating stages, four cards, a question-mark motif, accent lines and the reference's topic or colors are not mandatory.
A study with one indivisible question, a tutorial or a narrow slide edit does not require invented subquestions or an unrelated framing page.
Reflow or split when the canvas and substantive questions need more room; do not shrink text to preserve the example grid.
An unsupported causal chain must not be copied from the reference or inferred merely from related topics.
validation: The audience can identify why the study's question arises, state the main question and distinguish each source-supported subquestion.
The diagram's components and relationships match the source, with proposed pathways labeled and no invented objectives or implied results.

The actual render preserves a dominant question, readable supporting text, role-based anchoring and stable retained-text positions, work-area bounds and any section navigation's separate 12 pt minimum.
Illustration editing limits and native text, framing and connector editability receive separate review; subquestion cues are not treated as research evidence.

rules.name: Outline, visual storyboard and native construction
rules.trigger: Creating or substantially rebuilding a research presentation.
rules.decision: Develop the narrative, design each page's visual explanation, then reproduce it as actual slides. Substantive introduction pages use rich illustrated explanations with sufficient scientific detail.
rules.execution: Follow visual-storytelling.md#outline-then-storyboard-then-build. Specify source-supported objects, states, operations or comparisons, evidence, labels, supporting text and composition before authoring. Adapt concept, question, significance and contribution compositions to the study. Use detailed scientific illustrations and analytical graphics beyond the bundled icon vocabulary. Preserve the storyboard's explanatory substance in the finished slides.
exceptions: A narrow edit does not require rebuilding the whole deck.
Covers, contents, dividers and justified exact-text or mathematics pages have distinct purposes. Never invent data or relationships to fill a visual design.
validation: Each introduction page lets the audience see the relevant phenomenon, contrast, question or significance with sufficient supporting detail.
The native slides realize the storyboard rather than substituting sparse headlines, generic text flowcharts or decorative icons.
Actual science determines layout, counts and detail; reference compositions do not force identical cards or fixed chains.

rules.name: Accurate diagram connections
rules.trigger: Creating or changing a diagram with connectors.
rules.decision: Connect the intended source and target with the correct semantic direction and a clear visible attachment.
rules.execution: Follow visual-storytelling.md#connect-the-intended-objects. Record edge meaning and endpoint objects, choose suitable ports, reroute after final node placement and check native renders. Respect authoring endpoint conventions, group transforms, visible contours and image padding. Vertically center node text under R016.
exceptions: Association or unresolved relationships may use nondirectional links or explicitly proposed connections when supported.
The bounded preservation helpers do not implement automatic semantic routing; use native authoring and report unavailable application checks as pending.
validation: Every arrow tip reaches the intended visible boundary with deliberate clearance and no label penetration.
Direction, branch junctions, crossings and feedback paths are unambiguous after native export.
Moved or resized nodes trigger endpoint and routing rechecks.

rules.name: Scholarly slide attribution
rules.trigger: Displaying research citations or reference entries on slides.
rules.decision: Use APA 7 author-year citations and bibliographic structure with italic slide reference text, keeping routine extraction-page lists out of the visible composition.
rules.execution: Follow writing-style.md#slide-citations-and-references. Place concise attribution by its evidence and complete verified entries in the reference section. Use the private ledger or notes for detailed source locators. Entire-line italics are palate's slide style, not a universal APA typography requirement.
exceptions: Retain necessary direct-quotation locators, required credits and bibliographic publication page ranges or article numbers.
Unknown date, publication status or metadata must not be invented to complete a reference.
validation: Visible citations identify the correct work and correspond to complete reference entries.
Reference text is italic and readable, with no routine source-extraction page-list footer.
Scientific source mappings, required credits and consequential uncertainty remain preserved.
